brief: Gasoline futures are up about 30% since early August, retail diesel is nearing $6/gallon, and one-year inflation swaps are back near their highest level since mid-June. BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky argues these elevated consumer prices are catching up to the discretionary sector, which shows a negative year-over-year return despite the S&P 500 up about 18% year-over-year, with apparel, leisure/travel, and homebuilders all showing vulnerabilities. He extends the caution to other pockets: private equity and credit managers, which rallied from early July, have stalled and are rolling over again, and the equal-weight S&P 500 ex-AI just posted its worst day in two months and its worst drawdown since May. Even the semiconductor index's recent ~9% rally hasn't reclaimed its 50-day moving average, which Krinsky likens to the SOX's six-month topping process in 2000 before its September breakdown. His conclusion: a correlation-one downside event is brewing.
